restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type must be both finite and nonempty; the statement does not cover an empty family.

The denominator can be zero, for example when every coefficient is zero or if LocalDef004 μ X evaluates to zero. Lean's real division is total, so division by zero evaluates to zero rather than making the proposition undefined; the right side then becomes 2.
Although every admissible scale used in LocalDef009 is required to be nonzero and finite, an infimum of such scales can still be zero.
LocalDef003 redundantly requires measurability and positivity outside LocalDef006 even though LocalDef006 repeats both conditions.
Measure.real is a total ENNReal-to-Real conversion. Under the probability-measure hypothesis the event measure is finite, so no infinity-conversion anomaly is expected on the left side.
The theorem separately assumes integrability and zero integral of each X i; these are not included merely by the exponential-scale predicate at the syntactic level of the target.
ambiguities: The proposition asserts only existence of a positive absolute constant c and does not identify its value or optimality.

The scale LocalDef004 is defined through an ENNReal infimum followed by toReal and a finite supremum; the proposition does not state within its target that this construction agrees with any separately named conventional norm.

Independence is the library predicate ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun, whose exact semantics are mediated by the displayed kernel definition rather than restated as elementary event-factorization conditions.
No positivity assumption is placed on LocalDef004 μ X or on ∑ i, (a i)², so the totalized zero-denominator cases are genuinely included.

binders: There exists a real constant c.
Universally quantify over a finite, nonempty index type ι and a measurable sample-space type Ω.
Universally quantify over a probability measure μ on Ω and a family X : ι → Ω → Real.
Universally quantify over real coefficient functions a : ι → Real and real thresholds t.
hypotheses: For every i, X i satisfies LocalDef003: it is measurable and there exists a real K > 0 satisfying LocalDef006 μ (X i) K.
Expanded, LocalDef006 requires X i to be measurable, K > 0, the function ω ↦ exp((X i ω)²/K²) to be integrable under μ, and its integral to be at most 2.
For every i, X i is integrable under μ and has integral exactly 0.
The indexed family X is mutually independent under μ in the sense of ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun.
conclusions: The real-valued μ-measure of {ω | |∑ i, a i · X i ω| ≥ t} is at most 2 · exp(-(c · t²)/(LocalDef004 μ X)² · (∑ i, (a i)²)⁻¹), equivalently as parenthesized in the target, 2 · exp(-(c · t²)/((LocalDef004 μ X)² · ∑ i, (a i)²)).
The same positive constant c works uniformly for every permitted finite nonempty family, probability space, independent centered coordinate family, coefficient vector, and nonnegative threshold.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef003 μ X means: X is measurable and there exists K > 0 such that LocalDef006 μ X K holds.
LocalDef006 μ X K means: X is measurable, K > 0, exp(X²/K²) is integrable under μ, and ∫ exp(X²/K²) dμ ≤ 2.
LocalDef009 μ X s, for s : ENNReal, means: X is measurable, s ≠ 0, s ≠ ∞, exp(X²/(s.toReal)²) is integrable under μ, and its integral is at most 2.
LocalDef008 μ X is the ENNReal infimum of all s satisfying LocalDef009 μ X s, and LocalDef005 μ X is definitionally this same value.
LocalDef004 μ X is the finite supremum, over every i in ι, of (LocalDef005 μ (X i)).toReal.
The weighted sum is ∑ i∈ι a i · X i(ω), and the coefficient energy is ∑ i∈ι (a i)².
The left side uses Measure.real, namely conversion to Real of μ applied to the tail event.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive real constant c such that, for every finite nonempty family of mutually independent, integrable, mean-zero real random variables whose exponential-square moments are controlled, every real coefficient vector a, and every t ≥ 0, the probability that the absolute weighted sum |∑ i a i X i| is at least t is at most 2 exp(-c t²/(Kmax² ∑ i a i²)), where Kmax is the maximum over coordinates of the infimum admissible exponential-square scale defined by LocalDef009.
